summary: Go's pmdoc reader reads bare web addresses and emails as remark-gfm reads them as a whole: micromark's autolink-literal tokenizer at every position it starts an address (inside goldmark's inline parse, the guard asked at every unescaped ASCII punctuation character and searching each run to the next question, with goldmark's text splits joined back so document weight is unchanged), then mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal's transform (URL pass, then email pass) over decoded text runs at block close, weighed as autolinks. goldmark's own linkify parser leaves the reader, the writer's `http\:` escape is deleted, and the email rows flip once INFRA-530 (mailto: href) is on main.

decisionsForArchitect: Scope: the plan takes the whole class of positions for web addresses and emails (non-ASCII or digit previous, ], |, !, character references, line or cell opening with punctuation, x;www.), not only the listed rows. Recommendation: keep it.
INFRA-530 dependency: the email rows need INFRA-530's mailto: href on main; the branch takes main on the conflict INFRA-530's merge makes in linkify_test.go, and INFRA-531 merges after INFRA-530.
Plain-text addresses in a tree (typed in the live editor, ask text) read back as links in Go, as the engine already reads them; accepted, no migration of stored documents.

findings.finding: Seven of the ten rows are read by the engine's tokenizer, not by remark-gfm's transform; the two readers end URLs differently (x;https://x.test/a_ b vs see http\://x.test/a_ b; x;https://a.test/*b* c), and the ten rows cannot tell them apart.
findings.answer: The plan reads with both readers (departure 1) and adds discriminating rows to the Go test and the e2e test (A2).

findings.finding: goldmark never asks Go at these positions; adding triggers splits text nodes and changes document weight (PR #2094's revert, growth_test.go:39-40 pins More. at 4); a post-parse pass cannot undo emphasis the tokenizer would have claimed.
findings.answer: Design 1: new punctuation triggers plus a run search inside goldmark's parse; the guard records each split it causes, elementInlineCounter does not charge it, and a three-argument CloseBlock joins it back, so the weighed tree is main's (A4, with a negative control).

findings.finding: Links made outside goldmark's tree would not be weighed; escapes inside them would stop being counted.
findings.answer: Design 2 makes transform links nodes of goldmark's tree at block close, weighed as autolinks; a new node kind joins weighed, the README table and TestEveryNodeOfTheSchemaWeighsWhatItMakes.

findings.finding: Making see http\://x.test a link changes how every stored plain-text https\:// reads; the escape becomes dead; typed URLs stay plain in the live tree; joined edits may be newly refused; asks gain links.
findings.answer: Departure 3 deletes the escape; Consequences names each effect (typed URLs, asks, joined edits, stored documents, no migration) for the architect; T2 adds an ask round-trip test and a stale plain-URL edit/accept test.

findings.finding: Is the fix the ten rows or the whole class with the same cause?
findings.answer: The whole class (departure 2), with class rows in the Go test, the corpus document and the differential corpus; named for the architect as decision 1.

findings.finding: Emails at the same positions, and coordination with INFRA-530.
findings.answer: The architect added seven email shapes to the spec; the plan reads emails with micromark's email tokenizer and the transform's email pass, removes goldmark's linkify parser, and sequences after INFRA-530 (T5, decision 2).

findings.finding: Links Go makes over decoded text need decoded label and href (www\.x.test, character references).
findings.answer: Design 2's rule: parse.go gives a transform link its decoded label and href.

findings.finding: Writer rules and pinned renderings are tied to Go's current reading; the differential's churn and lost-fixed-point gates will fire.
